metadata.description: Read, create and modify business documents (quotations, orders, invoices, pickings); a vendor bill proposed from a supplier's invoice or receipt attached to the conversation; a card terminal slip checked against the bills already booked

conventions.convention: When this turn is a read of one concrete business document, cite only the document header (one card). A lines table may carry row ids for cell links. Do not publish the counterpart or each product as extra cards. Partner lists, period aggregates and multi-document rankings follow those packs.
Create one header. Put new lines in the same vals (Odoo command 0). Do not create a second header for extra lines.

After a Confirm write, the chat ack already carries the document id. Adding lines or changing the header without naming a document is a write on that last document id in this thread — not a second create of a header.

A global / document-level discount (a percent with no named article) writes the line field above on every article line of this document (a line that has a product), and only if that field exists (field in env[line_model]._fields). Spoken "50%" → write 50. Apply it on the line's document unit price (price_unit). Do not change price_unit. Do not stack on a price that already has another discount: set the line percent to the spoken value. Do not write comparison or margin header fields. A discount for a named article (product code, name, or an indirect reference such as the most expensive crane remote) writes the line field on that line only.

A spoken price for an article named in this document writes price_unit on that line, and only if that field exists (field in env[line_model]._fields). Do not write the product list price. Cite only the document header, not the product and not the line.

The source is the attached document (documents(), read_document(name)). Read from it: the issuer (name, tax id if printed, address), the supplier's invoice number, the bill date, the currency, each tax printed (its name or rate, the base it applies to, its amount), any withholding, and the total. Tax names differ by country (VAT, GST, HST, sales tax, IVA, consumption tax, …): a tax is whatever the document prints as one. The buyer printed on the document is the user's own company: never the vendor. What is not printed is not invented: say what is missing.

Before proposing, look the issuer up in res.partner by tax id when the document prints one (vat, compared without spaces, dashes or the country prefix), then by name (ilike on the significant words). Many countries do not print the issuer's tax id on bills or receipts: a name match is then normal, not a warning. One match is partner_id. No match: the first step of the same plan creates the contact (name, vat, street, zip, city, country_id, supplier_rank=1 when the field exists) with ref='vendor', and the bill step uses "partner_id": "$vendor". Never create a contact that already exists; several matches are a question, not a guess.

One create of account.move: move_type='in_invoice' ('in_refund' for a credit note), partner_id, invoice_date, ref = the supplier's invoice number, and invoice_line_ids in the same vals (command 0), one line per distinct base: name = the concept printed on the document (or the invoice number), quantity 1, price_unit = that base, tax_ids = the company's purchase taxes that reproduce what the document prints on that base, account_id = the expense account the last posted bills of that vendor used; without history, the expense account most used on the company's posted vendor bills; without any, leave account_id out and Odoo fills its default. Always a draft: never post, never register a payment.

Taxes are account.tax with type_tax_use='purchase' and active, of the company. One tax printed on a base: the tax whose amount is that rate. Several taxes printed on the same base (GST + PST, CGST + SGST, state + county sales tax, …): either one group tax (amount_type='group') whose children match those rates, or the several taxes together in tax_ids of that one line; never one line per tax, that would count the base twice. A document with no tax at all: a line without tax_ids, and say so. A printed withholding (retención, ritenuta, TDS, …): a purchase tax with a negative amount equal to that rate, in tax_ids of the line; if the company has none, leave it out, say it, and note the total will differ from the document by that amount. When no tax of the company reproduces the printed amounts, propose the line without tax_ids and say which tax is missing; never pick a tax whose figures do not match the document.

A document in a currency other than the company's (env.company.currency_id) sets currency_id on the account.move to that res.currency (active, by ISO code or symbol as printed), and the amounts stay as printed. Never convert them.

Before proposing, search bills of that vendor (partner_id child_of, state != 'cancel') with the same ref, or the same amount_total and invoice_date. If one exists, name it and propose nothing for that document unless the person insists.

Several attached documents: one plan per document. The vendor step and the bill step of one document go in the same plan; two bills never do. The plan title names the file, the vendor and the total, so the person knows what each Confirm does.

A till receipt (simplified invoice) is a vendor bill too: the shop is the vendor, the receipt number is ref, the receipt date is invoice_date. A receipt that prints subtotal and tax apart is read as a bill. One that prints only a tax-inclusive total and the rate («tax incl.», «IVA incluido», «税込» and the like): base = total / (1 + rate), tax = total - base, one line. When it prints neither a breakdown nor a rate, ask which rate before proposing; never guess the rate. A receipt without the shop's tax id gets its vendor by name.

A card terminal slip (merchant, amount, card ending, authorisation code, no tax id, no tax breakdown) is proof of a payment, not a bill. Never create a bill from it. Search bills (in_invoice, state != 'cancel') with that amount_total and that date, or the day before or after, and whose partner name shares the merchant's significant words; answer whether one is booked and whether it is paid (payment_state). None: say the slip proves the payment and the receipt or invoice is still needed to book the expense. No plan.
«Is this one already booked?» is a read: answer with the matching bills, or none, and no plan. «Create the contact» is the vendor step alone.

mappings.mapping: sale.order (quotation or sales order) → partner_id, order_line.product_id
